methodological_rigor.justification: This is a multi-center single-arm open-label phase I/II trial (LOKON003, NCT04123470) with a formal Bayesian Optimal Interval (BOIN) dose-escalation design at two dose levels (1×10^11 and 5×10^11 VP). Primary endpoint was tolerability; efficacy endpoints (PFS, OS, DCR) are explicitly labeled as post-hoc, which weakens inference. The biomarker analyses use appropriate methods (NanoString with RUV-4 and Benjamini-Hochberg; Olink with paired t-tests), but subgroup survival analyses (by dose, injection site, M-stage, prior therapy lines) were small (n=7 vs 17), lack multiplicity correction, and are used to generate rather than confirm hypotheses. The dose imbalance in enrollment (7 vs 17) and baseline M-stage imbalance (71% M1a at lower dose vs 41% at higher) is acknowledged as a confounder but not analytically addressed.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: ICI-refractory stage IV melanoma with limited options has a clinically meaningful ORR of 17%, DCR of 54%, and 24-month OS of 46%, suggesting genuine activity for a population where chemotherapy yields ~6 months OS. Safety was favorable (only 2 grade 3 DLTs; no grade 4/5 attributed events). These findings support continued clinical investigation but the small sample size and dose-cohort imbalance limit conclusions. Corresponds to Oxford LoE 2b for a single-arm phase I/II trial.

reporting_quality.justification: Reporting is generally thorough for a phase I/II trial: clinicaltrials.gov registration, IRB approvals, inclusion/exclusion, BOIN design, adverse events per CTCAE v5.0, RECIST 1.1 response assessment, ADA measurement, biomarker methodology, and Kaplan-Meier/Cox analyses. Source Data files are provided for all figures and a study protocol is in Supplementary Data 1. Post-hoc status of efficacy analyses is explicitly labeled. CONSORT would be the primary standard for a trial; no explicit CONSORT checklist is cited.

novelty_literature.justification: LOAd703 is a novel oncolytic adenoviral vector encoding trimerized membrane-bound CD40L and 4-1BBL. This is the first clinical report of LOAd703 in melanoma (prior report was in pancreatic cancer, ref 20) and in combination with atezolizumab in the ICI-refractory setting. The mechanism (intratumoral TME reprogramming delivering costimulatory ligands, avoiding systemic CD40 agonist toxicity) is biologically innovative, and the coupling with multimodal biomarker profiling (NanoString PanCancer Immune, Olink IO, Oncology II) adds mechanistic depth. Not paradigm-shifting, but a meaningful first-in-indication phase I/II contribution.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized with clear sections, appropriate tables for demographics, response, and adverse events, and mechanistic figures (heatmaps, volcano plots, Kaplan-Meier curves). The discussion appropriately contextualizes the data against TIL therapy (Chesney, Rohaan), real-world chemotherapy benchmarks, and approved oncolytic products (T-VEC, nadofaragene firadenovec). Writing is clear; minor grammatical issues and some dense paragraphs. Interpretation explicitly flags post-hoc and small-sample caveats.

key_strengths: First-in-indication phase I/II of LOAd703 plus atezolizumab in ICI-refractory stage IV melanoma, with promising 46% 24-month OS
Favorable safety profile: only 2 grade 3 DLTs, no grade 4/5 LOAd703-attributed AEs, MTD not reached
Comprehensive mechanistic biomarker package (NanoString TME panel + Olink IO/Oncology II) showing Th1 activation and rational ICI co-target upregulation (CTLA-4, TIGIT, LAG-3)
Rational design rationale for intratumoral delivery avoiding systemic CD40 agonist hepatotoxicity
Source Data provided for all figures and study protocol in supplement
key_concerns: Single-arm design without randomized comparator; efficacy inference limited
Dose-cohort imbalance (n=7 vs 17) with baseline M-stage imbalance (71% vs 41% M1a) confounds the notable 1×10^11 dose OS advantage
PFS, OS, DCR explicitly post-hoc and sample-size-driven subgroup analyses are under-powered
Biomarker subgroup contrasts (above vs below median OS) did not survive multiplicity correction; authors report uncorrected results for 'hypothesis generation'
Intratumoral lymph-node injection associated with worse OS (10 vs 35 months) is an unexpected signal warranting prospective exploration
chief_reviewer.rationale: A well-reported first-in-indication phase I/II with mechanistic biomarker depth and clinically meaningful outcomes in a difficult population; tier 2 (e.g., Nature Communications, Journal of ImmunoTherapy of Cancer, Clinical Cancer Research scope) is defensible with minor revisions addressing dose-cohort imbalance and making post-hoc nature more prominent.
